```{r setup}
library(bssd)
```

```{r helpers, include = FALSE}
res_file <- function(folder, name) {
  system.file(folder, "results", name, package = "bssd")
}
read_results <- function(folder, name) {
  read.csv(system.file(folder, "results", name, package = "bssd",
                       mustWork = TRUE), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
fmt <- function(x, digits = 4) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
fmt_e <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1)
count_of <- function(tab, j) sum(tab$judgement == j)
```

## Model

Brock et al. (2023) estimate the posterior probability that the event
probability per unit time on study drug, \(\pi_d\), exceeds that on control,
\(\pi_c\), in an ongoing blinded study. Each subject with time at risk
\(t_i\) has the event with probability \(1 - (1 - \pi)^{t_i}\) on the arm
received, and the likelihood of the blinded data is the mixture over the two
arms weighted by the randomization probabilities. The prior of \(\pi_c\) is
the meta-analytic predictive (MAP) prior from historical control arms,
\[
\pi_j \mid a, b \sim \mathrm{Beta}(a b N, (1 - a) b N), \quad
a \sim \mathrm{Beta}(1/3, 1/3), \quad b \sim \mathrm{Beta}(5, 5),
\]
where \(N\) is the total number of historical subjects, \(a\) is the mean
event probability and \(b\) discounts the historical information. The prior
of \(\pi_d\) is Beta(1/3, 1/3).

`map_beta()` integrates the posterior of \((a, b)\) by quadrature, which
gives the MAP prior as a mixture of Beta distributions, and `mapbern_post()`
integrates the two-dimensional posterior of \((\pi_c, \pi_d)\). Brock et al.
(2023) use Stan for both steps and fit a mixture to the MCMC draws of the
MAP prior. The likelihood is that of the exponential Bernoulli mixture model
(`expbern_post()`) with hazards \(-\log(1 - \pi)\); only the priors differ.

## Example

```{r map}
prior <- map_beta(events = c(9, 11, 10), n = c(100, 100, 100))
attr(prior, "moments")
nrow(prior)
head(prior, 3)
```

```{r fit}
set.seed(2)
n <- 200
drug <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.75)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, ifelse(drug == 1, 0.18, 0.095))
fit <- mapbern_post(y, t = rep(1, n), k = 3, prior_c = prior)
fit
```

A prior derived with the RBesT package can be used as well: the rows `w`,
`a` and `b` of a `mixbeta` object are the columns `w`, `shape1` and
`shape2` of `prior_c`.

```{r rbest, eval = FALSE}
# mix: a mixbeta object of the RBesT package
prior_c <- data.frame(w = mix["w", ], shape1 = mix["a", ],
                      shape2 = mix["b", ])
```

## Numerical integration and comparison with MCMC

```{r check, include = FALSE}
v <- read_results("validation", "validate_methods_python.csv")
vm <- v[grepl("^PY_MAP", v$id), ]
j <- read_results("validation", "validate_jags_methods.csv")
jm <- j[grepl("^J2_MAPBERN", j$id), ]
```

Against independent Python computations (dense composite Gauss-Legendre
rules split exactly at \(\pi_d = rr_0 \pi_c\) for `mapbern_post()`, and a
dense grid over \((a, b)\) for `map_beta()`), the largest absolute
difference of the `r nrow(vm)` compared quantities is
`r fmt_e(max(vm$abs_diff))`. A JAGS model with the mixture prior and latent
treatment assignments gives:

```{r mcmc-table, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(data.frame(quantity = jm$quantity, MCMC = fmt(jm$reference),
                        bssd = fmt(jm$bssd), judgement = jm$judgement),
             align = "lrrl")
```

## Reproduction of Brock et al. (2023)

```{r repro, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
f <- res_file("reproduce", "reproduce_Brock2023.csv")
if (nzchar(f)) {
  b <- read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  cat("`inst/reproduce/reproduce_Brock2023_simulation.R` repeats the ",
      "simulation of Tables 1 (common events) and 3 (rare events) for the ",
      "heterogeneity levels None and High (1000 trials per setting), and ",
      "`inst/reproduce/reproduce_Brock2023.R` compares the mean of the ",
      "posterior probability: ", count_of(b, "PASS"), " PASS, ",
      count_of(b, "EXPLAINED"), " EXPLAINED and ", count_of(b, "FAIL"),
      " FAIL of ", nrow(b), " settings.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat("The simulation of Tables 1 and 3 (`inst/reproduce/",
      "reproduce_Brock2023_simulation.R`) has not been run for this ",
      "installation.\n", sep = "")
}
```

## References

Brock, K., Chen, C., Ho, S., Fuller, G., Woolfolk, J., McShea, C. and
Penard, N. (2023). A Bayesian method for safety signal detection in ongoing
blinded randomised controlled trials. *Pharmaceutical Statistics*, 22(2),
378--395. <https://doi.org/10.1002/pst.2278>
